title: Flashcards
summary: Decks of cards with spaced repetition, reminders, stats and CSV import
description:
Flashcards helps you remember anything with spaced repetition, on your phone and offline.

**What it does**

- Make decks and cards with a front, a back and an optional hint you reveal only when you need it. Your decks are colourful tiles: each deck's icon gives it its colour, and a bar shows how much of it you have studied.
- Study a deck: read the front, show the answer, then tap **Again**, **Hard**, **Good** or **Easy**. Each button shows when you will see the card next.
- The schedule is a classic spaced-repetition method: cards you know well come back after days, then weeks, then months; cards you forget come back the same day and grow more slowly.
- Each deck shows how many cards are due and how many new ones are waiting. You set how many new cards come in per day.
- Undo your last answer, edit a card mid-session, pause a card or reset its progress.
- A study reminder per deck, on the days and at the time you pick, or one daily reminder for all decks instead, sent only when cards are due.
- **Stats**: your streak, the days you studied this week, cards answered today, how much you remembered over 30 days, learned and well-known cards, a 30-day chart, a study calendar, a 14-day forecast and your answer mix.
- A home-screen widget shows how many cards are waiting.
- Import and export CSV: bring decks along, or keep a backup.
- In English or Slovak, following your phone's language.

**Bring your decks with you**

Imports decks exported as text or CSV: one card per line, front and back separated by a comma, semicolon or tab, with column names such as front and back, question and answer, or term and definition. A deck column sorts cards into decks (new decks are created), and simple formatting such as line breaks and bold text is cleaned up. Without a line of column names the first column is the front and the second the back, and lines starting with # are skipped.

**What it never does**

No ads, no paywall for study modes, no account and no internet access: the app cannot reach the network at all. Your cards and progress stay in this app's own storage on your phone. Files leave only when you export them to a place you pick.

Not yet: pictures and sound on cards.

research.used_for: Deck settings people expect: new cards per day, maximum reviews, learning steps, a starting ease of 2.50, an easy bonus of 1.30 and a hard interval of 1.20.

The four answer buttons (Again, Hard, Good, Easy) and how they move the ease (-20, -15, 0, +15 points, never below 130%); every new interval at least a day longer; why the newer FSRS model needs fitted parameters.
The SM-2 algorithm the schedule follows: ease starts at 2.5, never below 1.3, intervals grow by the ease after each correct answer.
The box-based alternative that was considered: simpler, but every card in a box gets the same gap, so it adapts less to hard cards.
Statistics people use: today's answers and correct rate, future due forecast, review calendar, card counts by stage, answer button counts, retention.
Study reminders per deck, sent only when cards are due.
People want a study streak and a reminder before they lose it.
What low-star reviews complain about: study modes moved behind a paywall, lost decks, missing export; what people want: free spaced repetition, unlimited cards, easy backup.
Free tiers that limit study rounds per day and show ads during study.
Export format A (notes as plain text): one note per line, fields separated by a tab, HTML formatting kept in the fields.

Export format A, continued: newer files start with #key:value lines (#separator:tab, #html:true, #deck column, #tags column); separators comma, semicolon or tab; quoted fields may hold line breaks; HTML entities such as & and  .
Export format B (copy of a study set as text): term and definition separated by a tab, rows by a new line, no header line.
Export format B, continued: custom separators can be typed in for term/definition and for rows, so files vary.
